note: Iluka Supply Agreement (Oct 2022): binding contract for 30,500 t of contained TREO within a 20-30% xenotime concentrate (total_tonnes is contained TREO, not concentrate mass); Iluka takes 100% of product up to a 5,500 tpa TREO maximum with right of first refusal on excess. Delivery by road from first concentrate (2028). RISK: certain conditions precedent (NTU financing/FID, Iluka financial close) passed their satisfaction dates as at Sep 2025, entitling either party to terminate; neither has, and extensions are under discussion (pp.5, 91-92).

Strategic partnership includes a conditional post-FID equity commitment: Iluka may subscribe for ~A$53M of Northern Minerals equity via placement and put/call options, subject to positive FID, secured project funding, Iluka due diligence and continuation of the Supply Agreement (p.86).
Iluka scenario: ~15 ktpa for more than 25 years. High confidence this is the intended pathway; project itself remains pre-production.

Heavy mineral concentrate requires further processing in the Northern Territory or Western Australia; specific refinery not publicly established. Insufficient evidence to assert Fingerboards -> Eneabba.

15-year offtake structure covering the four magnet rare earths announced April 2026; USAR names future Serra Verde concentrates as planned oxide-production feedstock. No evidence material has yet physically flowed.
Inferred from USAR's stated integrated mining-to-magnets strategy; internal flow within the USAR platform.
Inferred from USAR's stated integrated mining-to-magnets strategy; internal flow within the USAR platform.

Separated oxides -> metals/alloys -> magnets is a functional dependency only; no offtake, metallisation or magnet-production counterparty identified. Iluka's FID release (p.2) names rare-earth metallisation as a potential future step; NTU DFS (Fig 41, p.74) shows a 'potential Iluka metallisation plant (study in progress)' and ex-China magnet producers / Western OEMs as the intended market.

The refinery will be fed initially from Iluka's own Eneabba monazite/xenotime stockpile, giving an indicative nine-year refinery life on the stockpile alone with project NPV > A$500M under that conservative scenario (p.2). Owned feed - not dependent on any third-party mine.

Same refinery and already in Iluka's hands, so a Browns Range disruption does not stop Eneabba producing. Caveat: the stockpile is monazite-dominant (LREE-rich) with a xenotime component; its Dy/Tb contribution relative to Browns Range's concentrate is not quantified in this source, so it is an alternative for refinery throughput more than for heavy rare-earth volume.

Australian Government risk-sharing arrangement: A$1,050M non-recourse loan to RefineryCo under the A$2B Critical Minerals Facility administered by Export Finance Australia, plus A$200M cost-overrun facility; BBSY + 3%, tenor up to 16 years; royalty to Iluka up to A$81M/yr capped at A$900M (pp.1-2). Debt, not equity.
Agreement announced April 2026 for Serra Verde to combine with USA Rare Earth; not modelled as completed ownership.
Uses the same downstream refining infrastructure (Eneabba), so a Browns Range disruption could be mitigated without a new refining pathway.
Already producing Dy/Tb-bearing material, unlike the Australian projects; relies on a separate (USAR) downstream pathway rather than Eneabba.
Significant potential Dy/Tb output in an allied jurisdiction, but downstream pathway is unresolved; that uncertainty should lower its ranking, not be hidden.
